chapter_title: Concerning the Ad[vent] of the Apostle.
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation
 of the Kephalaia
 Selections


---


**
¶3.
** Understand
, my
 beloved:
 All divine
 emissaries who
 are from
 time to time sent down
 into
 the natural state
 of
 humanity
 are
 like those
 who cultivate spiritual ground
; and
 the
 receiving
 communities they
 gather
 are like two
 distinct
 states
 of
 spiritual
 harvest —
 one being
 the ing
athering of interior truths that
 have
 rip
ened, the
 other the
 ing
athering of good
 works brought
 to
 full
ness.
 For the state
 in
 which interior truths reach
 mat
urity does
 not persist
 through
 every
 phase
 of spiritual
 development; nor does the state in which
 works
 are
 gathered.
 Rather, each
 state
 arrives
 according
 to its own order, as
 those
 who cultiv
ate know
 the
 lesser
 kn
owledges proper
 to each
 phase
,
 and know
 when
 they
 are ready to be
 received
;
 and they tend these
 kn
owledges through
 successive
 states
 until
 the
 works
 themselves
 come
 to full
ness.

---


**¶4.** Now
 the
 one
 who cultivates spiritual
 ground lab
ors in the
 state
 of rip
ening interior truths; for
 if
 he comes and sows some interior
 truth
 there, he
 shall be engaged
 from the very
 beginning with
 that
 seed
 and
 labor
 over
 it. Yet when the state
 of spiritual
 warm
th comes in
 its
 cycle
, and
 his
 interior tru
ths reach
 the
 full
ness of their
 maturity, then the cultiv
ator comes
 forth and g
athers them. Even so
, the one
 who tends
 per
ceptions lab
ors from
 the beginning
 over
 good
 works; he
 tends the
 per
ceptions and nur
tures what
 grows
 from
 them, and when
 the
 works
 ri
pen he
 comes forth and gathers them from
 the living
 perception
 that
 bore
 them.


---

**¶6.
** And
 in
 this
 manner
, through
 long
 ages of
 preparation
 before
 the descent
 into
 the natural state, the divine
 emissary
 journ
eys down
ward into
 the world of
 appearances
 and
 first
 liber
ates the spiritual essences of his
 receiving
 community in
 the celest
ial realm
,
 fre
eing them
 from bond
age to the merely
 natural person
 —
 those
 spiritual
 identities whose
 forms he had already
 released
 in
 the heights.

---

**
¶7.** Like the cultivator
:
 when
 he begins
,
 he tends the ground
 from
 the
 first
 moment
 of s
owing,
 so
 that
 when the state
 of interior
 rip
eness arrives
, he may gather what
 has
 mat
ured;
 and in
 the other
 season
 he
 lab
ors for
 the gathering
 of works that
 have come
 to fullness.

---

**
¶8.** Again, this
 is
 how the divine emissaries operate
 from
 the very
 origin
 of humanity's spiritual
 formation:
 as I have said
, before
 all
 things the
 em
issary
 first
 liberates the spiritual essences above
, in
 the celestial state
.


---

**¶9.
** Yet when the
 community
 is
 born into
 the natural
 condition
, the
 emissary desc
ends to
 it and at once receives
 it into
 the infl
owing
 truth
 that
 proceeds
 from the Divine
,
 and by
 which
 it
 is elevated
 toward
 the infinite
 good
ness. He remains
 present
 in the natural
 state for
 the appointed
 duration
, corresponding to the phase
 when
 the world reaches
 its appointed
 full
ness; and when
 that
 state
 m
atures, he is raised up out
 of the natural
 condition
.
 He leaves
 his spiritual
 community in
 the world
 and de
parts. Still, he continues
 to sust
ain and aid
 his community
 from
 within
. Whoever among
 them
 passes
 out
 of the
 ou
termost natural
 form after
 him —
 he becomes for
 them a gu
iding presence
 and a fore
runner; he
 goes
 before them into
 what
 lies
 beyond, while
 others
 remain
 established
 in natural
 life
. He is the one who becomes for
 them a helper and a guardian from
 the spiritual world; he does
 not withdraw
 his
 influence
 in
 secret, until his
 community compl
etes its full
 transformation
.
 When
 his community has been wholly
 gathered
,
 he is raised
 up after it, and enters
 the celest
ial kingdom
.
 And
 he r
ests in
 joy
 and peace
 at the last.

---

**
¶10.** Like the cultiv
ator who is glad of
 heart when
 he brings
 in the harvest of
 mat
ured tru
ths.
 Or like one
 who acqu
ires spiritual
 goods,
 who
 returns
 from
 the
 natural
 state with the dou
bling of all
 that
 he carried
 —
 the abundance
 of goods
 and truths multipl
ied through faithful
 use.

---

**¶
11.** When the divine emiss
ary is raised up from the natural
 state
, he and his community together
 —
 for every em
issary is
 like
 a
 living
 perception
 still
 laden
 with its first works
:
 even
 as the r
ipe works
 are gathered, new
 ones are
 propagated in
 their
 place
 and
 come
 to maturity in their
 own
 season. At
 no
 time is the perception
 bare
 of good
 works!
 Rather, even
 as the rip
ened ones
 are gathered, new works
 come
 forth
 and
 appear
 upon
 the extending
 branches of
 that
 perception. The
 cultivator g
athers whatever
 has reached
 full
ness.
 And
 the one
 who tends the spiritual
 ground does not rest
 at
 any time from the labor
 and the suffering
 of
 cultivation
. At
 what hour may he cease? Only
 when the
 last
 interior
 truth is
 gathered in the
 season
 of its
 rip
eness!
 For
 those
 tru
ths s
own in the cold
 and
 bar
ren states
 of spiritual
 winter
 become
 the
 works
 that
 grow
 up
 in
 states
 of spiritual warm
th and are
 gathered in the full
ness of their season
.

---

**¶12
.** The divine emissaries operate
 in
 the
 same
 way. When
 one
 em
issary is raised up into
 the celestial states
, he and his community, and they
 depart from the natural condition —
 at that very
 moment another emissary is sent down
 to a
 new community
.
 Yet first he
 liber
ates the spiritual essences of his community
 in the celestial realm, as
 I have said
. And
 then
 he too desc
ends and manif
ests himself in the natural state, and
 he
 releases
 his community and
 saves it from bond
age to evil
 and falsity.

---

**
¶20.** Like a perception
 that is stripped
 bare
,
 and the works upon
 it taken away. And it remains behind
,
 devoid of any good.


---

**¶23.
** Yet when the spiritual
 community entered
 into
 the natural condition, the appointed
 state
 arrived
 for
 the redemption of souls — like the
 season
 in
 which interior
 truths reach
 their ripeness and
 are ready
 to be gathered.


---

**¶24.
** He unveiled to me the interior
 divine truth, the truth
 that is hidden from all
 external
 states of
 mind
 and all
 successive
 ages
 of
 the
 church
 —
 the truth concerning
 the lowest
 natural depths
 and the highest celestial heights. He
 unveiled to me the truth of
 wisdom
 and falsity; the truth of the
 devast
ation of opposition
, the
 warfare
, and the great assault
 that fals
ity spread
 throughout
 all
 things
.
 And
 afterward
 he unveiled to me also
: how
 wisdom
 entered
 into falsity, and through
 their
 com
mingling this
 entire
 created
 order
 was established
.

---

**¶25
.** He opened my understanding
 also
 to the way that doc
trinal forms
 were
 constructed — vessels
 of teaching in
 which the divine principles
 of
 wisdom might
 d
well, so
 as
 to separate
 and
 purify whatever
 is of
 wisdom
 from the whole
 of
 creation. And
 conversely, the resid
ue of
 evil
 and the
 effluence
 of falsity are
 cast
 down
 into
 hell
.
 He
 revealed to me the forming
 of the
 earliest
 spiritual
 humanity.
 He also instruct
ed me concerning
 the perception
 of reasoning
 from natural
 evidence alone
, from
 which
 the
 earliest
 humanity
 received
 knowledge
;
 and their
 understanding
 was
 opened.


---

*
Note
 on
 a
 resistant
 image
:
* The two
 Egyptian
 months
,
 **
Parmuthi** and **
Paophi**, correspond
 to two
 distinct spiritual seasons
 —
 one for
 the harvest
 of interior truths (
sign
ified by grain
), the
 other for the harvest of good
 works (signified by fruits). Their
 altern
ation represents the truth
 that
 the spiritual life
 proceeds
 through ord
erly states
:
 tru
ths must
 ri
pen and
 be received
 before works
 of
 charity
 can be brought
 to full
ness,
 and this
 cycle never
 ce
ases while
 humanity
 end
ures in
 the
 natural world
.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Understand, O my beloved ones: All the apostles who are on occasion sent to the world resemble farmers; while their churches, which they choose, are like Parmuthi and Paophi. For, the way Parmuthi occurs not in all the months of the year; nor does Paophi [occur] in all of them. Rather, the season [is appointed] for it alone, as they know [the season of] its vegetables [and] the time they are cropped; also the vegetables and the [fruits of the] season; and they tend and ripen the pickings, and they [bring them] to Paophi.

Of course, now that farmer [labors in] Parmuthi; in that, if he will come and sow some corn seed there [to bring forth] cereal. And he shall be involved from the beginning [with] a corn seed and toil for it. Yet, when the summer comes each year, and his corn comes to the season of its harvest; then the farmer comes forth and harvests it. Even the gardener from the beginning [also] shall toil for his fruits; and he tends them and he [waters them,] and they ripen; and he comes forth and picks them from the tree.

Again, this too is [how] the apostles [work] from the beginning of the moulding of humanity [in the world], as I have told you, that when they [are sent,] before every thing he shall [make the forms of his church] free above, first.

Like the farmer who shall be glad of heart in [the season when] he was bringing in (the harvest). Or like the merchant who shall come up from a country with the doubling of his great cargo; and the riches of his trading.
Like a tree will be plucked, and the fruits on it taken away. And it remains behind without fruit.
Yet, when the church assumed the flesh, the season arrived to redeem the souls; like the month of Parmuthi that cereal shall ripen in, to be harvested.

He opened my eyes also to the way that the ships were constructed; to enable the gods of light to be in them, to purify the light from creation. Conversely, the dregs and the effluent [are cast down] to the abyss. The mystery of the fashioning of Adam, the first man. He also informed me about the mystery of the tree of knowledge, which Adam ate from; his eyes saw.

Also the way [the apostle lab
ors] many years before [he desc
ends to] the world, as he
 journeys below to the [world,
 he] makes the form of his church
 free, and [frees it from
 the body] of the flesh, whose
 forms he had made free [above in
 the heights.]

Like the farmer, for
 when he will [sow, from
] that moment he shall begin [to
] tend [it. When] it
 reaches Parmuthi also,
 he may harvest it[; and he
 shall] toil for the fruits of
 Paophi [also.]

Yet, when it [will be] born in the flesh, he shall come down to it and at once [...] it in the [...] which comes out from the [...] is raised up to the greatness. He shall continue in the world at this time [...] him, corresponding to the season when the world will come to his [...] when the season will mature he is raised up from the world [...] and he leaves his church {behind} and goes forth. Still, he [...] and he helps and aids his church. Whoever comes out from their body after him, he shall become for them a support and a leader; and he goes on before them [...], excepting the others who are set firmly in the flesh. He is the one who will become for them a helper and a guardian; he shall not take [...] in secret, until his church [...] change it [...] when his church [...] he was raised up after it, and went into the land of glory. And he rejoices and rests at the last [...]

When the apostle will be raised up from the world, he and his church [...] for every apostle [...] in the [...] Since [...] tree, that still is laden with its first fruits [...], and they are picked; they shall propagate other ones there, and they mature to the season to bring them forth. There is not any time the tree is bare of fruit! Rather, instead, those about to ripen as they pick them shall propagate other ones there. When they bear these [...] them on the tree; they come up and are brought forth upon its branches. They shall pick from it those that mature and ripen. The farmer does not rest at any time from the labour and the pain. At what hour may he cease? When he can finish harvesting the corn in Parmuthi! [...] them in the winter, the fruits of the summer shall [...] grow up and be picked in the month of Paophi.

The apostles are like this also. Now, when the apostle will be raised up to the heights, he and his church, and they depart from the world; at that instant another apostle shall be sent to it, to another church [...] it [...]. Yet, first, he shall make the forms of his church free in the heights, as I have told you. When [...]; again, he too shall come down and appear [...] and he releases his church and saves it from the flesh [of sin ...]
